title: Count a word in a sentence
description: A sentence is a text whose words are separated by single spaces; there is no other punctuation. Count how many of its space-separated tokens are exactly equal to the given word. The comparison is case-sensitive and whole-token only: "theory" does not contain the word "the", and "The" is not "the". Consecutive spaces produce empty tokens, which never match. The word is never empty (the Zehn version states this as a precondition). An empty sentence has no matches.
notes: Whole-token matching (not substring) and case sensitivity are the traps. The word is never empty.
